protagonist.who: You are one of three siblings at a chaotic weekend wedding on a sprawling family estate; the story moves through all three sibling viewpoints, and you are always the sibling currently in the room.
protagonist.wants: to get through the weekend with the family still a family and the estate's future honestly settled
protagonist.can_do: choose what to say or withhold, examine and pass documents, make promises or apologies, sign or refuse when a document is offered, and move between the estate's rooms
protagonist.cannot_do: know what the other two siblings know, open the inheritance papers alone, or settle any claim without the executor, the other siblings, and the people in the room hearing it

arena.description: The sprawling family estate and the small town it overlooks, the wedding weekend's single setting.

pressure.description: The ceremony is in a few hours and the executor has set the inheritance papers to be opened at the reception, so every conversation and document in the estate moves toward that reading.
pressure.clock_or_stock: none tracked: the weekend is told through wedding milestones (rehearsal dinner, ceremony, reception), because 3-0c names no failure trigger

opposition.who_or_what: the estate's executor and the other two siblings, each holding a different interest in the estate
opposition.wants: the executor wants a clean legal closure before the ceremony; each sibling wants their own claim, apology, or future recognized
opposition.means: they control the papers, signatures, guest list, seating, and the rooms where people can be overheard; they can include or exclude you from the rooms where a claim is made

mediation.question: Which of the family's secrets, grudges, or inheritance claims do you surface, and which do you keep in?

to_reach_pole_a.pole: surface: bring a secret, grudge, or claim into the open
to_reach_pole_a.what_you_must_do: in the current sibling's viewpoint, pick one unresolved item that sibling knows, find the person, document, or room that makes it count, and say or sign it where another sibling or the executor must answer
to_reach_pole_a.cost: the answer changes who trusts whom, and the item you leave unsurfaced hardens into resentment or a stronger claim

to_reach_pole_b.pole: keep in: soften, concede, or hold it back
to_reach_pole_b.what_you_must_do: in the current sibling's viewpoint, take one unresolved item out of the open: get the other person to lower their voice, get the executor to table a paper, or make a private concession, then carry it into the next room without letting it be repeated
to_reach_pole_b.cost: the truth stays under the table and the sibling who held it carries the weight, while the family's peace may be bought with a lie or omission

levers: a sibling's phone with the family group thread

turns.situation: You are the eldest sibling in the study when the executor brings the late parent's sealed letter and the inheritance papers, with the rehearsal dinner guests an hour from arriving.
turns.what_you_must_do: find out what the sealed letter says before the executor offers it to the wedding party

ways_through.way: you learn it from the executor, who reads the first line aloud
ways_through.cost: your private apology to the middle sibling is now known to the room

ways_through.way: you learn it from the middle sibling, who has already opened the envelope in the hallway
ways_through.cost: the middle sibling now knows you were waiting for the executor to decide for them

ways_through.way: you learn it from the papers, because you broke the seal
ways_through.cost: the executor sees the broken seal, and the letter can no longer be read as a private message

turns.situation: You are the middle sibling in the dining room as the executor posts the guest list and seating cards for the ceremony; the youngest sibling is asking to be seated with the estate caretaker, and the eldest sibling wants the inheritance papers read before the vows.
turns.what_you_must_do: get the seating decided before the ceremony cards are printed

ways_through.way: the youngest sibling is seated with the estate caretaker, because you gave the executor the seating card
ways_through.cost: the eldest sibling sees you favoring the youngest sibling's claim, and your apology is left out of the card

ways_through.way: the eldest sibling is seated at the head table, because you signed the executor's signature book for the head table
ways_through.cost: the youngest sibling is seated with the guests, and your private room is no longer available for the letter

ways_through.way: the seating is left as the executor wrote it, because you asked the executor to table the cards
ways_through.cost: the youngest sibling carries the unanswered question into the ceremony, and the eldest sibling assumes you chose silence

turns.situation: You are the youngest sibling at the reception when the executor opens the inheritance papers and offers the signature book; the eldest and middle siblings are both in the room, and the sealed letter is on the table.
turns.what_you_must_do: get the inheritance papers answered before the reception ends

ways_through.way: the papers are signed, because you placed the executor's signature book in the eldest sibling's hand
ways_through.cost: the middle sibling's claim is signed over without their voice, and your apology is lost in the signing

ways_through.way: the papers are tabled, because you gave the executor the sealed letter and asked for a private room
ways_through.cost: the eldest sibling leaves the reception believing you chose the middle sibling's silence over the family's future

ways_through.way: the papers are read aloud, because you handed the executor the family heirloom as proof of the claim
ways_through.cost: the middle sibling hears the truth in front of the guests, and the eldest sibling's grudge hardens into a claim

complications.description: The executor's signature book already contains a line signed by the eldest sibling, dated before the rehearsal dinner.

cast_seeds.wants: a clean legal closure before the ceremony begins
cast_seeds.holds: the inheritance papers, the sealed letter, and the signature book

cast_seeds.wants: their claim and apology recognized in the room
cast_seeds.holds: the knowledge of the eldest sibling's desire to read the papers before the vows

cast_seeds.wants: to be seated with the estate caretaker and their private claim acknowledged
cast_seeds.holds: the presence in the dining room and the reception room where the papers are opened

cast_seeds.wants: the inheritance papers read before the vows
cast_seeds.holds: the authority of the eldest sibling and the knowledge of the sealed letter's contents

cast_seeds.wants: to maintain the estate's physical order and their own role within it
cast_seeds.holds: the estate caretaker's position and the seating cards for the ceremony
